method: Each cited official URL was opened directly in this session; published values were compared with what the page currently shows. No value was copied from a search result, and no value was adjusted, averaged or inferred. Where a published value could not be reproduced it is marked discrepancy, not corrected by guesswork.

records.claim: The canonical injury page cites nfl.com/injuries/league/2026/REG10 as the 2026 Week 10 official report.
records.published: S01 = https://www.nfl.com/injuries/league/2026/REG10
records.observed: Page title: 'Official NFL Injury Report for Players - Week 10 of the 2026 Season'. Section heading: 'Injuries - WEEK 10'.
records.action: None. Title and heading agree for REG10.

records.claim: The REG9 URL is a correctly labelled earlier-week source.
records.published: Used earlier in the repository as the Week 9 report.
records.observed: Document title reads '... Week 10 of the 2026 Season' while the page heading reads 'Injuries - WEEK 9' and the first game is Thu Nov 5.
records.action: Cite REG9 only as 'WEEK 9 body, Week 10 document title'. Do not use its <title> to date a capture. Prior flag FLG-02 is reproduced here as still true today.
records.source_label: NFL official injury report, week 9 body / week 10 title

records.claim: The Week 10 report covers 14 games.
records.published: 14 games (dashboard games table and canonical matchup set)
records.observed: 14 team-pair sections on the official report (TNF WAS@NYG; NE@DET; KC@ATL; MIN@GB; JAX@TEN; BUF@NYJ; MIA@IND; CAR@NO; HOU@CLE; LAR@AZ; SEA@LV; SF@DAL; PIT@CIN; MNF LAC@BAL). The official Week 10 injury article also says 'all 14 games'.
records.action: None.

records.claim: The published capture contains 254 injury rows.
records.published: 254 rows
records.observed: Counting every player row currently shown on the official report gives 279 rows across 26 clubs, plus 2 explicit 'No Injuries Reported' sections.
records.action: Published count understates the current official report by 25 rows. Re-capture and republish; keep the old value labelled with its own timestamp.

records.claim: Seahawks: 'No Injuries Reported'.
records.published: 0 rows; explicit no-injury section for SEA @ LV
records.observed: 15 Seahawks player rows are listed for SEA @ LV (AJ Barner, Anthony Bradford, Charles Cross, Sam Darnold, Derick Hall, Drew Lock, Quenton Nelson, Uchenna Nwosu, Patrick O'Connell, Connor O'Toole, Brandon Pili, Jarran Reed, Rashid Shaheed, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Leonard Williams).
records.action: Do not publish a no-injury state for Seattle. Re-capture before any availability signal uses it.

records.claim: Bengals: 'No Injuries Reported'.
records.published: 0 rows; explicit no-injury section for PIT @ CIN
records.observed: 4 Bengals player rows are listed (Jonathan Allen, Kyle Dugger, Dylan Fairchild, DJ Turner II).
records.action: Do not publish a no-injury state for Cincinnati. Re-capture.

records.claim: Four clubs have 'No Injuries Reported'.
records.published: 4 sections: Seahawks, Bengals, Chargers, Ravens
records.observed: 2 sections: Chargers and Ravens ('No Injuries Reported', LAC @ BAL, Monday Nov 16).
records.action: Two of the four published no-injury claims are contradicted above (VR-05, VR-06). Publish 2.

records.claim: Six players carry a game-status designation (5 Out, 1 Questionable).
records.published: 6 designations
records.observed: The official Week 10 article designates 9 players: Commanders OUT Colson Yankoff (knee), Lucas Patrick (concussion); Giants QUESTIONABLE Malik Harrison (groin); Patriots OUT Ben Brown (knee), Carlton Davis (knee), TreVeyon Henderson (illness); Lions OUT Kerby Joseph (knee), Cade Mays (ankle), D.J. Reed (hip).
records.action: The 6 published designations match the Commanders/Giants/Patriots entries exactly; the 3 Lions designations are missing.

records.claim: Commanders OUT designations.
records.published: Lucas Patrick (concussion) Out; Colson Yankoff (knee) Out
records.observed: Article: 'OUT: TE Colson Yankoff (knee), C Lucas Patrick (concussion)'.
records.action: None.

records.claim: Giants Questionable designation.
records.published: Malik Harrison (groin) Questionable
records.observed: Article: 'QUESTIONABLE: LB Malik Harrison (groin)'.
records.action: None.

records.claim: Patriots OUT designations.
records.published: Ben Brown (knee), Carlton Davis III (knee), TreVeyon Henderson (illness) Out
records.observed: Article: 'OUT: OL Ben Brown (knee), CB Carlton Davis (knee), RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness)'.
records.action: None.

records.claim: Lions designations are blank, implying no designation.
records.published: Kerby Joseph, Cade Mays, D.J. Reed rows present with blank game status
records.observed: Article: 'OUT: S Kerby Joseph (knee), C Cade Mays (ankle), CB D.J. Reed (hip)'.
records.action: A blank game-status cell is being displayed where the official article states Out. Either populate the designation or mark the cell 'not captured'.

records.claim: Per-club injury row counts across the 26 clubs the site reports on.
records.published: 20 clubs with matching counts; Jaguars 10, Colts 11, Cardinals 13, 49ers 10; Seahawks and Bengals published as no-injury (0 rows).
records.observed: 26 clubs reconcile as follows: 20 counts match exactly; four understate the live report - Jaguars 11 (BJ Green II absent), Colts 13 (CJ Allen, Grover Stewart absent), Cardinals 14 (Andrew Wingard absent), 49ers 12 (Dre Greenlaw, Christian McCaffrey absent); Seahawks list 15 players and Bengals 4 rather than none. Total 279 vs 254 published.
records.action: No published row names a player who is absent from the official page, so the capture did not invent data - it dropped rows. Re-capture (see queue VQ-R01) and assert per-club counts before publishing.

records.claim: Green Bay Packers depth chart could not be parsed, so it is published as a coverage gap.
records.published: Failure reason: 'https://www.packers.com/team/depth-chart: no depth table parsed'
records.observed: packers.com/team/depth-chart publishes full Offense, Defense and Special Teams tables (44 published slots) dated 'Unofficial, Nov. 10, 2026'.
records.action: This is a false negative: the club does publish an HTML table. The published reason should not stand as evidence that no chart exists.
records.source_label: Green Bay Packers club depth chart

records.claim: Houston Texans depth chart could not be parsed.
records.published: Failure reason: 'https://www.houstontexans.com/team/depth-chart: no depth table parsed'
records.observed: houstontexans.com/team/depth-chart shows the heading 'Unofficial Depth Chart' followed by an image; no player table, no player names in text.
records.action: The parse result is correct. Reword the reason to 'published as an image only - requires manual or OCR review' so it is not read as 'no chart published'.

records.claim: Four clubs appear in depth data but not in injury data (Chicago Bears, Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles, Tampa Bay Buccaneers).
records.published: depth-only club labels
records.observed: The official Week 10 schedule lists exactly these four clubs under 'Teams on Bye'.
records.action: Explained: on bye, so no Week 10 injury report section. Record this as a known, benign coverage difference rather than an anomaly.

records.claim: Ravens depth: Lamar Jackson (1st), Tyler Huntley (2nd), Joe Fagnano (3rd) at QB.
records.published: published_rank 1-3 as listed
records.observed: The live club chart lists QB Jacoby Brissett, Joe Fagnano, Kedon Slovis. Jackson and Huntley are absent from the chart.
records.action: Two of the three published names are no longer on the club chart. Officially reported context: Jackson (right thumb) and Huntley (toe) were placed on injured reserve on Nov 5 and Brissett was acquired from Arizona on Nov 6.

records.claim: Colts depth chart row count is 57.
records.published: 57 rows
records.observed: The club article lists 57 player slots (25 offense, 24 defense, 8 special teams). The total matches only because two opposite defects cancel: one row merges two players and one row is a phantom duplicate.
records.action: A row-count check cannot validate this club. Validate by player name and position, not by count.

records.claim: Colts TE rank 4 row.
records.published: player = 'Will Mallory Pharaoh Brown'
records.observed: Article: 'TE: Tyler Warren, Mo Alie-Cox, Drew Ogletree, Will Mallory, Pharaoh Brown' - five separate players.
records.action: Split into 'Will Mallory' (rank 4) and 'Pharaoh Brown' (rank 5). Do not display merged names.

records.claim: Colts CB rows.
records.published: Two first-string CB rows: 'Charvarius Ward Sr.' and 'Charvarius Ward'
records.observed: Article: 'CB: Charvarius Ward Sr., Kenneth Harris' and a separate 'CB: Sauce Gardner'.
records.action: Remove the duplicate 'Charvarius Ward' row; keep 'Charvarius Ward Sr.' and 'Sauce Gardner'.

records.claim: Commanders depth sample (Terry McLaurin 1st at WR; Jayden Daniels 1st at QB).
records.published: published_rank 1 for both
records.observed: Live club chart: WR Terry McLaurin then Treylon Burks; QB Jayden Daniels, Marcus Mariota, Athan Kaliakmanis.
records.action: None for these rows. The chart also lists 'Frankie Luvu' with an empty second slot and 'Kain Medrano' third, so empty cells must stay empty rather than shifting later players up.

records.claim: Giants depth sample (Malik Nabers 1st at WR; J.J. McCarthy 1st at QB).
records.published: published_rank 1 for both
records.observed: Live club chart: WR Malik Nabers, Malachi Fields, Jalin Hyatt; QB J.J. McCarthy, Jameis Winston.
records.action: None for these rows.
records.source_label: New York Giants club depth chart

records.claim: Seahawks depth: one first-string WR.
records.published: Cooper Kupp and Rashid Shaheed both under WR at rank 1 (single cell)
records.observed: Live club chart shows both names inside one WR cell, followed by Irvin Charles in the next column.
records.action: The capture is faithful to the page. The display needs to distinguish 'two players share one published slot' from 'rank 1 followed by rank 2'.

records.claim: Replacement, rank and expected-snaps fields are blank because the official report does not establish them.
records.published: blank in every injury row
records.observed: The report gives player, position, injury, practice status and game status only. However, the NFL publishes dated starter changes separately: Drew Lock expected to start for Seattle (Darnold out), Kyle McCord in line for a first start for Miami (Willis on IR), Jacoby Brissett acquired and starting for Baltimore after Jackson and Huntley went on IR.
records.action: Blank is correct for the report page. Add a separate, dated 'announced starter' evidence field sourced from these NFL articles so a replacement can be shown as announced rather than inferred.
records.source_label: NFL: Darnold ruled out, Drew Lock expected to start

records.claim: Miami QB availability is unchanged week to week.
records.published: No Miami quarterback appears on the Week 10 injury report.
records.observed: NFL: Malik Willis was placed on injured reserve with a groin injury and Kyle McCord is in line for his first start; Willis is ineligible until the Dec 13 game against Chicago.
records.action: Absence from the weekly report is not evidence of availability when a player is on injured reserve. Availability features need a reserve-list feed, not only the weekly report.
records.source_label: NFL: Dolphins place QB Malik Willis on injured reserve

records.claim: Official transaction data is available to reconcile roster and availability changes.
records.published: No transaction feed is used anywhere in the canonical lab.
records.observed: nfl.com/transactions lists dated moves; for example Baltimore acquired Jacoby Brissett from Arizona on 11/06 and Ryan Neuzil from Atlanta on 11/10.
records.action: Add the official transactions page as a captured, dated source. It reconciles club-chart staleness such as VR-17 without inferring anything.

records.claim: Practice status and game status have defined official meanings.
records.published: Cited as the definition source for Questionable, Doubtful and Out.
records.observed: Official policy text: practice status is Did Not Participate, Limited Participation (less than 100 percent of normal repetitions) or Full Participation; Questionable means it is uncertain whether the player will play; Doubtful means unlikely to participate; Out means the player will not play. 'Probable' was eliminated because about 95 percent of Probable players played.
records.action: None. Note that 'Out' for a practice report was eliminated, so a game-status Out must be sourced to the game-status report, not the practice report.

records.claim: Market prices and historical odds are unavailable from official NFL sources for model benchmarking.
records.published: All line and correlation cells blank; S12 cited.
records.observed: NFL Support: the NFL widgets show odds, spreads and over/under numbers provided by official bookmaker partners (FanDuel, Caesars, DraftKings); bets are placed through a redirect to the bookmaker. The NFL does not present these as its own prices.
records.action: Keep market values blank. Obtaining a permissioned historical price archive remains a blocking decision, not a scraping task.

records.claim: Walk-forward validation is the stated method for time-ordered data.
records.published: Cited S14 (scikit-learn TimeSeriesSplit)
records.observed: TimeSeriesSplit provides train/test indices on time-ordered data 'where other cross-validation methods are inappropriate, as they would lead to training on future data and evaluating on past data'; successive training sets are supersets of earlier ones.
records.action: None. Gap 5 uses the same logic and must also group by game so that legs from one game do not leak across folds.

records.claim: Uncertainty is reported rather than claiming luck is removed.
records.published: Flag F06 and gate G06 state luck cannot be eliminated.
records.observed: NIST: a 95 percent confidence interval does not mean a 95 percent probability that the interval contains the true mean; the level is a property of the method. Interval width shrinks with sample size and grows with standard deviation.
records.action: None. Phrase results as an interval on a method, never as 'removed luck'.
records.source_label: NIST/SEMATECH confidence limits for the mean

records.claim: Tracking-based signals must use defined Next Gen Stats metrics.
records.published: Cited S09 for tracking metrics.
records.observed: Next Gen Stats glossary defines Completion Probability, Expected Completion Percentage, Aggressiveness (defender within 1 yard), Average Separation, Cushion, Time To Throw and related metrics.
records.action: None. Separation and completion-probability definitions are the defensible basis for a personnel-dropoff signal; they are not available in the current snapshot.

coverage_notes: Live re-checked in this pass: the Week 10 injury report (all 14 sections), the Week 10 injury article, the Week 10 schedule, the league transactions page, seven club depth pages (Commanders, Giants, Colts article, Packers, Texans, Ravens, Seahawks), the NFL odds-widget FAQ, the injury-policy article, the Next Gen Stats glossary, NIST confidence limits and scikit-learn TimeSeriesSplit.

Not re-checked live in this pass: the remaining 23 captured club depth pages, the NFL team directory, the 2026 rulebook, NFL game-day/stadium preparation, the AT-spotter page, scikit-learn calibration and GitHub Pages documentation. They are marked pending, not confirmed.
